subject: Community Conversation With Calvin Lindsey Jr
overview: The West Medford Community Center hosted its final Fresh Fridays program before a summer hiatus, featuring an interview with Emmy-winning filmmaker Calvin Lindsey Jr. and a jazz performance.

items.title: Introduction and Announcements
items.summary: Terry Carter opened the program with acknowledgments of the Medford Arts Council and reflections on the community center's 80th anniversary celebrations.

items.title: Poem: Neighborhood
items.summary: The host read a poem about the values and culture of the West Medford community to set the tone for the evening's conversation.

items.title: Conversation with Calvin Lindsey Jr.
items.summary: Filmmaker Calvin Lindsey Jr. shared memories of growing up in West Medford, the influence of neighborhood mentors, and his professional experiences producing the public television series Say Brother.

items.title: Discussion of Vitiligo Documentary
items.summary: Lindsey described his recent documentary project focusing on the personal stories and medical treatments of people living with vitiligo.

items.title: Lightning Round Reflections
items.summary: The discussion concluded with brief reflections on local figures and landmarks, including musician Phil Hamilton and photographer Aaron McDaniel.

items.title: Musical Performance by AJ and the Groove
items.summary: Anita Wood and her ensemble performed a set of jazz standards including 'East of the Sun', 'Besame Mucho', and 'Summertime'.

items.title: Closing Remarks and Community Updates
items.summary: The program concluded with announcements regarding upcoming Juneteenth celebrations at City Hall and the West Medford Men's Club barbecue.
